questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a czech friend living there, its cheap living there and a beautiful city. And its Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academic level a bit too low. Not much theoretical and too few powerpoints during lectures.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received emails and went to a introduction party and there was an introduction lecture as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy! I can strongly recommend
https://prague-shared-flats.eu/
because its very easy and convenient and you will live in a building with many Erasmus students and parties and meet a lot of people very easily.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can also be nice living in the dorms because you get close connections with other students living there. It's also cheaper than living in a shared flat. But it's far away from all the bars and thing going on in Prague (mostly in the city center). And living in a shared flat is better because kitchens have more equipment than they have in the dorms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty easy through the Erasmus program. The host university's webside was a bit confusing though (very oldschool design). But the people working at the faculty responded very quickly to the emails and was also very available on the phone.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As described above was the university staff very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted except from one which was not available in the fall semester but only in the spring.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it you will get most of the courses you want just email the professors and they will enroll you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting courses at first but the academic level was too low and the teachers didn't use powerpoints much (so it was just them talking for one and a half hour).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not very theoretical, nice that it was practical but i missed some more academic level it was almost like I only learned stuff I learned in high school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was nice that the format was hybrid during COVID-19 pandemic so you had the chance to show up on campus but could also stream the lecture live on Zoom.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Data Analysis in MS Excel
JEM221 Data Science with R I
JPM812 Democratic backsliding 
JTM267 Economy and Politics in the 20th Century Eastern Europe
Promoting democracy abroad the EU and US in third world countries
EU institutions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
JTM267 Economy and Politics in the 20th Century Eastern Europe
Advanced Data Analysis in MS Excel
JEM221 Data Science with R I
Promoting democracy abroad the EU and US in third world countries
Economic integration (I didn't enroll but my friends liked it a lot)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Spend some money on cafes because it was so cheap to eat brunch and buy coffee.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: public Transportation was much cheaper than I expected (40 DKK pr month) and the same for school books (0 DKK). Beer and drinks was also much cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university didn't offer any sports or other non-academic opportunities but there are so many Erasmus Whatsapp grous so it wasn't a problem finding tennis, bouldering, hiking or other sports opportunities in Prague (easier than in my home city Copenhagen).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None but instead I enjoyed bouldering, tennis, hiking, fitness and running so it wasn't a problem. I also found amny social and cultural activities through facebook and Whats app groups for Erasmus student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing Center Smichov (bouldering), Tennis with Erasmus student, going to the movies in prague 3, joining the light festival, using the cycle-boats on the river, doing ceramics at Skoutsky institut and Kreativni Zebra.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the national museum (both new building and old building), visit museum of communism, visit Meetfactory, visit Prague castle (especially the st vitus cathedral)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the young czech people speak way better english than I expected and they are super nice and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's pretty hard getting in contact with locals because there are no social activities at the university. So all social stuff is with Erasmus student. But talk to locals at bars or clubs and before lectures on campus and you will find out that they are super cool!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. Some older Czech people doesn't like expats but don't take it too personally.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that they are a post-communist country is very interesting and that they like beer and are very proud of their country and there history.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live in
https://prague-shared-flats.eu/
!!
Go on a lot of trips (e.g. hiking trips) to meet other Erasmus student outside of Prague
Go on a lot of trips to other countries e.g. Budapest or Krakow or Dresden. It's a very nice way to become closer friends with a smaller group of people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't study too hard before the political science exams (only the ones on institute of economics).
Try to explore all the hidden cafes and cultural places in the city.
In general just do a lot of stuff in your free time -stuff you never do or don't have the time and money for at home because it's too expensive in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
To get better in English
To meet so many nice and social people and get a big network in a new city (a felt like i knew more people in Prague than i do in Copenhagen).
To have such a rich every day live where I had the time and money to go out, do sports and explore the city.
T

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get a friend group that I could get closer with (I mostly hung out with new people every week which got quite exhausting sometimes)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
